prompt: Many major museums hold objects that were removed from other countries in the past. Some people believe these objects should be returned to their countries of origin, while others argue they are better preserved and more widely seen where they are. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
Many famous museums in the Europe and the America have the objects which were taken from the other countries in the past. Some people think that these objects must be returned to their original countries, but other people think that it is better to keep them where they are now. This essay will discuss the both opinions.

On the one hand, many people believe that the objects should go back. The main reason is that they were taken without the permission, often during the colonial period, so the original countries are the real owners. Moreover, these objects are the part of the identity of those countries, and the young generation should see them in their own country and not travel to the abroad. Also it is not fair that a country must pay the ticket to see its own history. Some of these objects are used in the religious ceremonies also, so for the local people they are not only the art.

On the other hand, the museums say that they protect the objects. They have the special equipment for the temperature and the humidity, and the expert staff who can repair the damage. In addition, the big museums in the capital cities receive the millions of visitors every year, so more people can learn about the different cultures. If the objects are returned, maybe only the few people will see them.

In conclusion, the both sides have the good arguments. In my opinion, the museums should return the most important objects, but they can keep the other objects and also make the copies, so everybody is happy.
title: Should museums return what they hold?
